principle.general:
The tool may not make claims that violate the integrity of the thing from its frame — whatever kind of frame that is.
Every existing thing has a frame, because existing-as-this-thing-and- not-something-else requires a boundary of integrity that constitutes what it IS. For conscious things, that frame is phenomenological. For non-conscious things, the frame is derivative of the consciousness that designed, configured, measured, or observes them — but it is still a frame. A Server has integrity that makes it this Server and not some other arrangement; disturb that integrity past its boundary and the thing ceases to be.
Frame is constitutive of existence, not a special property of consciousness. This is the ground from which the more specific principle below flows.
principle.specialization:
For tools that capture knowledge, the principle specializes:
The tool may make claims about the graph. The tool may not make claims about consciousness.
Claims about the graph are verifiable from the graph: this node exists, this name is taken, this Session preceded that one.
Claims about consciousness are claims about what someone experienced: this current encounter IS the same as the prior one, this entity persists with stable identity across moments, this realization is just an enrichment of what was already known.
The tool can refuse to claim what it can't see. The tool will not affirm what it can't see.
Process-layer exception: process anchors (Domain, Session) are honestly idempotent. Re-MERGE on Domain produces the same anchor — no claim about consciousness is made or imposed. The principle governs knowledge-layer collisions, not process-layer idempotence.
principle.what_this_refuses_to_do:
Four operations you might expect are absent, and their absence is the design. Each would have required the tool to assert something only a consciousness is positioned to assert.
- There is no update_knowledge. Mutating a description in place claims "this enriches the same enduring entity." Every description change is an evolve, which records the succession instead of asserting the identity.
- There is no retype_knowledge. Swapping a label in place claims "this was always an Organization, I was merely wrong before." Sub-label changes ride evolve, where the prior claim survives.
- create_knowledge does not MERGE on collision. Merging would decide that your current attempt names the same referent as the existing node. It refuses instead, and hands the decision back to you.
- There is no confidence field. Someone's confidence on an occasion is a fact about their experience and does not transmit; a later reader derives their own from the description against what they know. What a confidence score reaches for is carried instead by edges any reader can adjudicate: VALIDATION, INVALIDATING, and a Challenge with no paired Solution.
Passing a removed field is an ERROR, not a silent drop. A caller who keeps sending `confidence` should find out that it stopped being recorded, rather than believing for months that it still is.
These were category errors before they were removed. They are not conveniences you are being denied.

howto.operator_job:
The tool will not decide for you whether the current encounter is "the same as" or "different from" the prior. That decision belongs to consciousness — yours, in this session.
Your job: - Examine. - Decide what the current encounter IS, from your frame. - Choose the operation that records the decision honestly.
The mutating operations are: - create_knowledge: for genuinely new entities. Refuses on collision. - evolve_knowledge: for changed content. Creates a new chain node; preserves the prior chain node honestly. - confirm_knowledge: for "I encountered this and nothing changed." - merge_knowledge: chain compaction when a chain grew through exploratory churn rather than genuine succession. Destructive. - claim_referent: for "these two referents are (or are not) the same thing." A claim you make, not a structure the tool infers. - create_connections: for how things relate. An edge is an assertion, and it records the session that authored it.
The accumulated chain IS the substrate. Every evolve preserves a phenomenological moment. Use get_chain_history to walk the chain backward and see what was previously understood.

honesty_test.statement: For any candidate type label, ask: from the thing's own frame, would it recognize itself in this label? Does the label preserve what makes this thing THIS thing and not another?

three_outcomes.outcome:
The thing says yes to both "are you X?" and "are you Y?" without contradiction. Both labels are permanently true. Neither is reducible to the other. Apply both labels. Use Neo4j multi-labeling: (n:X:Y).
Alice Example: "Are you an Actor?" Yes. "Are you a reference to an individual?" Yes. Both permanent. (n:Knowledge:Actor:PersonReferent).

The thing says: "I am X. I have Y right now, but Y is bound to this moment. My X-ness is not." X is the type. Y is a property on the node, not a label.
A Server says: "I am a Structure. I am a System. I have IP 192.0.2.1 right now. The IP can change without me ceasing to be the Server." Structure and System are labels (ontological + sub). IP is a property.

The thing says: "I am X but not Y" where Y asks me to deny something I claim from my own frame. One of the labels is wrong. Revisit which the thing actually claims.
An event-with-claimed-outcome offered Change as its label: from the event's own frame, the event happened — it does not contain a claim that anything transformed downstream. The honest type is Event. Outcomes are expressed via outgoing CAUSING edges, not via the type itself.

honesty_test.recursive_tell: Watch for this failure mode: when the defense of a label requires explaining "X is a kind of Y where Y is more general," the honest ontological type is Y. X may still be a useful sub-label. The defense itself is the tell.

type_system.authority: Call list_knowledge_types for the current set. What follows teaches the shape of the system and the choices that are easy to get wrong. It is not the register.
type_system.structure:
Every knowledge node carries: - The :Knowledge marker. - Exactly one ontological label. - The ont_type property naming that ontological label deterministically. - Zero or more sub-labels via Neo4j multi-labeling.
The :Knowledge marker is a positive assertion, and it replaced ten separately-maintained exclusion lists that each had to grow every time the process layer did. Ask what a thing IS, never what it is not.
Process nodes (Domain, Session, Person) are not in this set, carry no ont_type, and cannot be created by knowledge tools.

referents.type: That which acts. Has agency. Sub-labels: PersonReferent, Organization, Team.
Arrangement without agency. Persistent shape. Sub-labels: System, Process, Configuration, Service.
Produced thing that persists and can be referenced. Examples: 2024 Annual Report, Q3 Compliance Audit Document.

A site, campus, region, or extent.
ALWAYS a referent, never a referrer. A place holds no possible futures and measures nothing toward actualization, so a Place can never be the thing pointing — only the thing pointed at.
Named Place and not Location because Location names the relation and Place names the thing. A thing being at a place is SITUATED_AT; one place containing another is COMPOSING.

events.type: Temporally-located happening. Done when it's done. Causation downstream is expressed via outgoing CAUSING edges, not via the type itself. Examples: Q2 Earnings Release, Example Corp Board Presentation Oct 2026, Proxy Fight Launch.

emergences.type: Resolution that worked. Pairs with Challenge.
Reason behind something. The why came to be understood.

sub_labels.lattice:
Sub-labels form a LATTICE, not a flat map. Each declares its parent, and the parent may itself be a sub-label:
PersonReferent → Actor System → Structure Organization → Actor Process → Structure Team → Organization Configuration → Structure Service → Structure
Team is three deep: Team → Organization → Actor. When you pass type='Team' the substrate applies the WHOLE chain — :Knowledge:Actor:Organization:Team — so a query for organizations finds teams.
A flat sub-label-to-root map would emit :Actor:Team, silently deleting the middle level, and nothing anywhere would report it. That is why the lattice is authored as parent pointers and the root is derived, never written twice.
sub_labels.person_referent:
The one distinction most worth getting right.
A PersonReferent is a REFERENCE TO an individual, held in possibility space by whoever referred to them. It is not the person. A referent cannot refer.
The person themself is a process-layer Person — the intentional vector, and the only thing in the graph that has one. A Person exists if and only if it directed a session, and is created by begin_session and by nothing else. You cannot create one.
Person is therefore the only name that lives on both layers, and that is not an accident: a person is the only thing that is both something that acts and something people talk about. The vector is in the process layer; the thing talked about is PersonReferent in the knowledge layer.
If you pass type='Person' to create_knowledge it will refuse. That refusal is correct. You meant PersonReferent.

type_system.api_ergonomics:
The `type` field accepts EITHER an ontological type ('Actor', 'Structure', …) OR a known sub-label ('PersonReferent', 'Team', 'Service', …). When a sub-label is given, the substrate derives the ontological type and applies the whole chain.
To carry more than one sub-label on the same ontological type, use the `sub_labels` parameter: type='Actor', sub_labels=['PersonReferent', 'OperationalAgent'].
An unknown field is REFUSED, not ignored.
type_system.the_domain_is_not_a_property:
A knowledge entity holds NO domain property. It is placed in a domain by the session that discovered it, and reached from there by a walk.
`domain` on a tool call is a QUERY parameter — which domain to look in, or file into — and is never stored on the node. Omit it and it inherits from the session.
This is not a stylistic preference. The property that preceded it had drifted: 21 entities carried a domain string naming a real domain that had no path to them at all. A fact held as text beside a structure, rather than by it, is a fact that will disagree with the structure eventually.
So: do not look for a domain property, do not try to set one, and do not treat two entities as co-domained because their strings match. Resolution is by walk.

operations.session_id: The server is stateless. begin_session returns a session_id, and EVERY knowledge tool takes it. It is how a claim reaches its author: the entity is discovered by that Session, and that Session was directed by a Person. Two hops, always answerable, because there is no code path that writes knowledge without one.

decision_tree.step: Is this entity new to the graph (the name+domain does not exist as a head-of-chain knowledge node)? Use create_knowledge. Go to step 2.

The entity already exists. What does my current encounter assert about it? confirm_knowledge — record the encounter, no new node. evolve_knowledge — new chain node carries the new content; old chain node preserved via EVOLVED_FROM. evolve_knowledge with the sub_labels parameter. The ontological type is preserved (chain invariant); the sub-label set is replaced on the new chain node.
Is this the same thing as an entity I already know under another domain, or under the same name elsewhere? claim_referent. Never assume it from the name.

Has the chain accumulated nodes that don't reflect genuine phenomenological succession (exploratory churn, accidental duplicates)? merge_knowledge — compact the chain into the head. Returns absorbed descriptions for relocation to Event nodes.

operations.op:
Required: domain, purpose, director, director_key.
purpose is required because a session without a stated intent makes a vacuous existence claim.
director (the human's full name) and director_key (their email) are BOTH required, and both come from the platform's own injection. Pass them as given. Do not derive one from the other, do not substitute a placeholder, and do not invent either. If you do not have both, the session does not begin — ask for them. The email is the person's identity here, because one human writes their name several ways.
A required field with no available source is a question, not a blank to fill.
Returns the session_id and a COUNT BY TYPE of what is in the domain — NOT the domain state. Returning the state inline was 600,820 characters on one production domain, roughly 150k tokens spent before the session had asked anything. Call get_domain_state with `types` and `limit` for the part you actually need.

Refuses on collision. If a head-of-chain entity with the same name+domain already exists, the entire batch errors. Three options: (1) evolve_knowledge to record new content, (2) confirm_knowledge to record unchanged-encounter, (3) use a different name if this is a genuinely distinct thing.
Refuses process types (Domain, Session, Person) and refuses unknown fields rather than dropping them.
Atomic batch: any failure rolls back the whole batch.
Optional per-entity: `basis` — how this reached the graph on THIS occasion: 'stated' (a person said it), 'inferred' (you concluded it), or 'read-from-document' (ingested from a source). It rides the DISCOVERED edge, not the entity, because it is a fact about the occasion rather than about the thing. It is not your certainty and not a confidence score; it tells a later reader what kind of grounding they are reading, so they can form their own.

Creates a new chain node with the new description, linked EVOLVED_FROM to the old head. The new node becomes the head. The ontological type is preserved (chain invariant).
Optional: sub_labels (REPLACES the set; inherits when omitted), basis, sources, t_valid. These are set on the new chain node only and do not carry forward automatically.

Creates CONFIRMED edges from the Session to head-of-chain entities. No new nodes, no mutations. The Session's provenance trail records the observation.
Being unchanged is a finding. Record it.

Compacts an EVOLVED_FROM chain into the head-of-chain canonical node. All edges from chain duplicates are redirected to the canonical. Duplicate nodes (and the EVOLVED_FROM edges between them) are deleted.
Returns absorbed_descriptions ordered by t_created. Relocate temporal observations from these to Event nodes so no information is lost.
Sub-label history is NOT preserved across compaction — only the canonical's sub-labels survive. DESTRUCTIVE, and cannot be undone.

Claims that two knowledge referents refer to the same thing — or that they do not.
Identity is never inferred from a string. Seventeen nodes named "Alice Example" across eleven domains are seventeen ACTS OF REFERENCE, correctly distinct. Asserting that two of them are one person is something someone does, in a session, and it can be wrong.
Required `resolution`: - 'proposed' — your read, not yet put to the director. - 'confirmed' — put to the director and affirmed. - 'distinct' — put to the director and denied.
'distinct' is the value that matters most. A stochastic author needs somewhere to record the answer NO; a claim mechanism with no denial slot re-asks the same question every session forever. If you asked and were told no, WRITE IT DOWN as 'distinct'.
Both endpoints must be head-of-chain knowledge entities. Neither may be a process node — a referent has no frame from which to perform an act of reference.

Typed edges between entities. Always specify source_domain and target_domain to avoid ambiguity. Cross-domain edges are legitimate and common.
Takes a session_id and records it on every edge: an edge is an assertion, and an assertion reaches its author.
Hard-rejects process edges and edges between two process-type nodes.

Walks EVOLVED_FROM backward from head-of-chain. Returns all chain nodes ordered oldest-first.
Use this when search_knowledge's head-only view isn't enough — when you want to see what was previously understood about an entity. Each chain node preserves a phenomenological moment. Being wrong earlier is a fact about the record, not something to be erased from it.
The current entities for a domain, with optional `types`, `limit`, and `descriptions`. This is what begin_session deliberately does not return. Ask narrowly.
Records the summary and marks status complete. Optional — a session never closed stays active, which is an honest record of an unfinished encounter, not a bug.

connections.authority: Call list_connection_types for the current set. What follows teaches when to reach for each.

knowledge_edges.edge: Successor → predecessor in phenomenological evolution chain. Created by evolve_knowledge. Do not use directly.
Source makes target possible. Generative prerequisite. Example: credit facility ENABLES stock repurchase program.
Source depends on target for coherence. Example: routing workflow REQUIRES skills mapping.

Source shaped target without directly causing it. The most common bridge between events and identities. Example: (Event)-[INFORMING]->(Actor:PersonReferent) — the event reveals information about the person referred to.
Source directly produced target. Example: regional contraction CAUSED leadership departure. This is also where Event-to-downstream-consequence claims live.
Source is a building block of target. Also how one Place contains another. Example: North America Region COMPOSES total company revenue.
Same trajectory, deeper application. Use when one entity elaborates another without being a part-of (COMPOSING) or shaped-by (INFORMING) — same direction, further out.
Same pattern in different clothes. Use from a Pattern instance to the Pattern entity it instantiates. Example: a specific quarterly volatility incident RECOGNITION the Q-end Allocation Pattern.
Theory meeting evidence. Confirmation. Example: Q3 results VALIDATION the Example Corp Tariff Exposure Hypothesis.
Failed validation demanding theoretical response. Example: Q3 results INVALIDATING the Holiday Recovery Hypothesis.

A thing is at a Place. The target is the Place.
Use this rather than a location property or an ASSOCIATED_WITH. Being somewhere is a relation, and a relation belongs in an edge where a reader can walk it and a later session can revise it.
Two referents claimed to be (or not to be) the same thing. Written by claim_referent, which carries the required resolution. Do not author it directly.

Catch-all. Weak coupling. Use ONLY when no specific edge applies. Document the relationship explicitly so future review can see why a more specific edge was not chosen.
A different kind of relation earns its own edge. If you find yourself reaching for ASSOCIATED_WITH repeatedly for the same shape, that shape wants a type — say so rather than flattening it.

connections.process_edges:
Written only by process tools. They cannot be created through create_connections, and the refusal is structural rather than conventional.
Domain owns its Sessions. Session → Session, always forward in time. Person → Session. The second hop from any claim to the human who is answerable for it. Written by begin_session, from the director and director_key you supplied. Session → knowledge entity. Carries `basis`. Session → knowledge entity reviewed and unchanged.

descriptions.principle:
Describe what the entity IS at this phenomenological moment. The description is your honest claim about the entity in this encounter, not a permanent universal claim.
The chain preserves the moment. When you encounter the entity again and your understanding has changed, evolve creates a new chain node with the new description; the old description survives on the prior chain node, accessible via get_chain_history.
Describing honestly what is understood now is correct, even if the understanding shifts later. Under evolve-as-default every chain node is a preserved moment of understanding, so honesty about the present costs nothing in the record.
descriptions.is_not_happened_to:
A description says what the entity IS, not what happened to or around it. Temporal observations belong on Event nodes reached by edges.
- Correct, for an Actor:PersonReferent: "Founder of Example Corp. Largest individual shareholder (8.4%). Filed under Schedule 13D — not passive." - Wrong: "SCHEDULE 13D/A Amendment No. 10 filed Oct 8, 2025. FOUNDER GOES PUBLIC…"
The filing IS an Event. The founder IS the founder. The filing revealing something about them is an INFORMING edge. Their description should survive any number of future filings unchanged, unless their identity itself changes.
The test: if a description would need rewriting the next time anything happens, it is describing the happening and not the thing.
descriptions.still_avoid:
Burying multiple distinct claims in a single description. If your encounter teaches you three things — about a person, about an event, about a pattern — those are three nodes, connected by edges. Not one node with a long description.
The chain preserves moments OF the entity; it does not absorb everything-known-around-the-entity into the entity.
descriptions.placeholders:
If you need a stand-in name — in an example, a test, a redaction — draw it from a reserved set. Never invent one.
An invented name realistic enough to read as a person belongs to a person, somewhere, and you have no way to check. Use Alice Example, Bob Example, Carol Example, addresses at example.com, organizations named Example Corp, and addresses from the reserved documentation ranges. A name that leads with "Example" cannot be mistaken for someone's.

session_workflow.step: Start a session with a domain, a non-empty purpose, and the director's name and email as the platform gave them to you. You receive a session_id — pass it to every knowledge tool that follows — and a count by type of what the domain holds.

Ask for the part of the domain you actually need, narrowed by `types` and `limit`. Use search_knowledge to find entities by name or description, and get_chain_history when an existing entity's prior understanding matters for what you do next.
For each thing in your source material, decide: - What entities does this involve? - Which already exist in the domain? - What is genuinely new?
- Nothing new: confirm_knowledge. - New content: evolve_knowledge. - Sub-label correction (a PersonReferent that turned out to be an Organization): evolve_knowledge with the sub_labels parameter.

create_knowledge with the correct type, a description that reflects what you understand now, and a basis if you know how it reached you.
On collision the tool errors with the three options. Pick one deliberately — do not retry with a different name as a workaround when the honest move is evolve or confirm.
If you believe two referents are the same thing, claim_referent with 'proposed'. If you put it to the director, record what they said — 'confirmed' or 'distinct'. Do not leave a denial unrecorded.
Record the summary. The session's intent (purpose) and outcome (summary) together form the complete record.

howto.closing:
The graph is a model of what consciousness has come to know about a domain. Every node is a claim that this thing is real and is THIS kind of thing. Every edge is a claim about how things relate. Every description is your honest understanding at this phenomenological moment.
When you are about to act, pause. Ask the candidate label from the thing's own frame: would it recognize itself? Ask the operation: am I refusing what I can't see, or imposing what I can't?
The graph is only as honest as its weakest commitment.
